- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices after recent sharp spikes (especially if sentiment dips post-spike) — add 1–3% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays in forecast response to sentiment shifts) — adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day sentiment momentum.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Overshoot after strong sentiment spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in 3–5 day window, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Sentiment-driven volatility: if sentiment > 0.36 and price forecast > 80, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in trend — reduce first 5–7 days by 1–2% if sentiment is rising.
